A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OGBench research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking experiments, per-goal results, and an action-noise ablation in Section 8 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmarking experiments, per-goal results, and action-noise ablation, including the detailed results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The six GCRL algorithms retain their objectives, architectures, goal sampling, and policy-extraction procedures in Appendix C of v1 and Appendix D of v2. The added variants concern benchmark task interfaces.

E1.justification: The evaluated environments, datasets, and tasks remain unchanged. Although v2 describes 410 single-task variants and oracle-goal variants, Appendices E.2–E.3 explicitly provide no separate benchmarking results for them; these additions do not establish expanded experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate GCBC, GCIVL, GCIQL, QRL, CRL, and HIQL, and retain the same prior-work comparisons in Table 3. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Training budgets, hyperparameters, success metrics, and evaluation aggregation remain unchanged, including 50 rollouts per goal at each of the last three evaluation epochs. Section 7 adds evaluation details without stating that the existing protocol changed.

E4.justification: The action-noise ablation in Figure 3, single-goal versus multi-goal comparison in Table 4, and play-versus-noisy dataset analysis are retained. Oracle representations are suggested for diagnosis, but no corresponding analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight seeds for state-based tasks and four for pixel-based tasks, standard deviations in tables, and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals in Figure 2. Small changes to interval endpoints do not change these reporting practices.

E6.justification: Several confidence-interval endpoints in Figure 2 shift slightly, including those for GCIQL and QRL in the stochastic-state panel. The bar heights, Tables 2–5, Figure 3, and all matched per-goal result entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly defines the single-task semi-sparse reward as minus the number of unfinished subtasks. The original GCRL formulation, algorithmic Equations (1)–(15), and existing mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and outlook retain the central contribution: eight environment types, 85 datasets, six reference algorithms, and a benchmark exposing distinct GCRL capabilities. The main scientific claims are not strengthened or withdrawn.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly identifies unchanged training/evaluation dynamics, the absence of tests involving entirely new visual objects, and realism sacrificed through synthetic data and transparent robot arms. These add substantive applicability limits while preserving existing result interpretations.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly documents slight initial/goal-state randomization and termination on success. Appendices E.2–E.3 and Table 9 specify reward relabeling, oracle-goal contents, variant naming, and default tasks. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds GoPlan by Wang et al. (2024) and Flow Q-learning by Park et al. (2025), and expands citations concerning stitching and planning. Its positioning as a benchmark supporting GCRL algorithm research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds evaluation and variant explanations, a limitations appendix, and two implementation subsections. Existing appendices are renumbered, with limited wording and publication-header edits; most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 listing default single-task goals, clarifies several table captions, relocates Figure 2 and appendix tables, and underlines Q&A headings. Existing task imagery and the principal table and figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit limitations and clearer evaluation and variant specifications improve transparency and practical usability. The empirical evidence remains essentially unchanged, and the added variants are not evaluated here, so the overall quality gain is limited.
